New CEO Enrique Lores, who took the helm on March 1, 2026 after running HP Inc. for nearly seven years, framed the reductions as part of a 2-to-3-year reorganization rather than a single-day workforce action. The company is targeting at least $1.5 billion in annualized run-rate savings within the same window. The announcement followed weaker-than-expected Q1 profit and confirmed Bloomberg and Wall Street Journal reporting that surfaced the night before. PayPal shares moved on the news as analysts reacted to the largest workforce reduction in the company's history. The "technology company again" pivot Lores pitched the cuts as a technology and culture reset rather than ordinary cost-cutting. In remarks captured by TechCrunch, he said PayPal is "becoming a technology company again" and that the company is "aggressively adopting AI in our development processes." His earlier all-hands message called for the team to "recommit to the fundamentals" and warned that PayPal had not invested enough in its core technology infrastructure during the prior leadership era. The two-part playbook he outlined: stripping out redundant management structures, and accelerating AI integration across engineering, support, and operations. Internally, that maps to flatter org design, fewer pure-management roles, and engineer/operator hybrid functions, the same template Coinbase, Cognizant, and Atlassian have already deployed under similar AI-restructuring rhetoric. "PayPal needs to focus. We need to recommit to the fundamentals." Enrique Lores, CEO, May 5, 2026 Why it matters This is the largest fintech workforce cut of 2026 by absolute headcount, surpassing Block (4,000, February) and dwarfing Coinbase (700, May 5), Bolt (250, April), and Crypto.com (180, March). PayPal joins a six-month pattern in which every major fintech reduction has cited AI as a primary or named driver. The "technology company again" framing in particular echoes Coinbase's "AI-native operating model" memo and Cognizant's "Project Leap" rhetoric, suggesting the AI restructuring vocabulary has now hardened into a template. The 2-to-3-year phased structure matters editorially. The 4,760 figure is a planned multi-year target, not an immediate RIF. There is no Q1 2026 WARN notice or 8-K specifying a near-term tranche, so the company will likely move workers out in waves over the next 24 to 36 months. Tracker readers should treat this as a structural commitment, not a Friday afternoon firing event. The deeper signal is the CEO swap itself. PayPal pulled Enrique Lores from HP Inc., where he led the company through its own AI repositioning. Picking an HP veteran to "rebuild" PayPal as a technology company is a bet that the printer-and-PC playbook for AI-era cost discipline now applies to consumer fintech. If it works, expect the same hire pattern in the next wave of mature tech CEO transitions.
